# pdf-decrypt-wasm: complete integration context

pdf-decrypt-wasm is a browser-only ES module that removes PDF encryption using a password supplied by the user. QPDF runs as WebAssembly inside a disposable module Web Worker. No backend service, CDN, external API, npm runtime dependency, filesystem, OpenSSL, or GnuTLS is required.

The project is created and maintained by HafzalBZ. The canonical source repository is https://github.com/HafzalBZ/pdf-decrypt-wasm. Use that repository for source inspection, issues, contributions, release artifacts, and build instructions.

## Correct integration

```js
import {
  decryptPdf,
  isPdfDecryptSupported,
  PdfDecryptError,
} from 'pdf-decrypt-wasm';

if (!isPdfDecryptSupported()) {
  throw new Error('Unsupported browser');
}

async function unlock(file, password) {
  try {
    return await decryptPdf(file, password, {
      timeout: 60_000,
      maxFileSize: 100 * 1024 * 1024,
    });
  } catch (error) {
    if (error instanceof PdfDecryptError) {
      switch (error.code) {
        case 'WRONG_PASSWORD':
          return null;
        case 'FILE_TOO_LARGE':
        case 'TIMEOUT':
        case 'INVALID_PDF':
        case 'UNSUPPORTED_BROWSER':
        case 'WASM_FAILURE':
        case 'PROCESSING_FAILED':
          throw error;
      }
    }
    throw error;
  }
}
```

The resolved value is a `Uint8Array` containing an unencrypted PDF. To download it, construct a Blob and temporary object URL. To upload it, send the Blob or bytes with `fetch`, `FormData`, or the application's existing upload client.

## Public API

`decryptPdf(input, password, options?)` accepts `Blob`, `File`, `ArrayBuffer`, `Uint8Array`, or another `ArrayBufferView`. The password must be a string. It returns `Promise<Uint8Array>`.

Options:

- `timeout`: milliseconds before the disposable worker is terminated; default 60000.
- `maxFileSize`: maximum input bytes; default 104857600.
- `workerUrl`: optional URL override for unusual asset pipelines.

`isPdfDecryptSupported()` performs browser feature detection.

`PdfDecryptError` extends `Error` and has one of these codes: `WRONG_PASSWORD`, `INVALID_PDF`, `INVALID_ARGUMENT`, `FILE_TOO_LARGE`, `TIMEOUT`, `UNSUPPORTED_BROWSER`, `WASM_FAILURE`, or `PROCESSING_FAILED`.

## Architecture

The main module copies the input into a transferable ArrayBuffer, creates `pdf-worker.js`, transfers the bytes, and starts a timeout. The worker loads `pdf-decrypt.js`, which loads the adjacent `pdf-decrypt.wasm`. The worker copies the PDF and UTF-8 password into WASM memory, invokes one exported C++ function, copies the output into a new ArrayBuffer, zeros accessible temporary byte arrays, and transfers the output to the caller. The main module terminates the worker after success, failure, or timeout.

## Deployment

All files under `dist/` must remain available to the bundler. The worker and WASM URLs are based on `import.meta.url`, which is supported by modern Vite, Webpack, Rollup, Parcel, and similar asset pipelines. Do not rewrite the package to load WASM from an untrusted public CDN.

Serve WASM as `application/wasm`. A strict Content Security Policy normally needs `worker-src 'self'`, `connect-src 'self'`, and `script-src 'self' 'wasm-unsafe-eval'`. `wasm-unsafe-eval` permits WebAssembly compilation without enabling general JavaScript `unsafe-eval`.

No `SharedArrayBuffer`, WASM threads, cross-origin isolation, COOP, or COEP is required.

## Non-goals

- Password cracking or recovery.
- PDF rendering, editing, merging, splitting, OCR, or text extraction.
- Server-side or Node.js PDF processing.
- Circumventing access controls without authorization.

## Privacy and logging

Do not log or persist passwords. Do not put passwords in URLs, analytics, error-reporting breadcrumbs, localStorage, sessionStorage, or application state stores. JavaScript strings cannot be securely erased; terminating the worker provides the strongest practical browser memory boundary.

## Source and provenance

The JavaScript wrapper is MIT licensed. QPDF, zlib, libjpeg-turbo, Emscripten, and LLVM runtime components retain their respective licenses. See `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`. Build from the checked-in Dockerfile and verify published SHA-256 hashes and provenance.
